items.title: Holonomic-constraint models of the force branch: constraint data, the constrained equation, virtual displacements and the scleronomic/rheonomic distinction
items.statement:
Adopt the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$ particle
labels with fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, a nondegenerate open time window
$I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$, an open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$
([[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (a)), and a force map
$$F:I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\longrightarrow(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$$
with the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of clause
(iii) of that postulate. Fix one inertial frame of the model with adapted
coordinates $(t,x)$ ([[post-cm01-frames]]), identify
$x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}=\mathbb R^{3N}$ with the position
tuple of the labels ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), and let $\mathsf M$ be the
mass operator of clause (d) of that definition, $\mathsf M(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})
=(m_{1}x_{1},\dots,m_{N}x_{N})$, a symmetric positive definite linear map with
block-diagonal matrix and blocks $m_{i}I_{3}$. All components below are read in
this frame, and dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]].

**(a) Constraint datum.** A **holonomic-constraint datum** on this data is a
triple $(O,k,G)$ with:

1. an **ambient set** $O\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, open and
   nonempty;
2. an integer $k$ with $1\le k\le 3N-1$;
3. a map $G=(G_{1},\dots,G_{k}):O\to\mathbb R^{k}$ of class $C^{2}$
   ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), each component carrying a
   declared dimension $[G_{\alpha}]=\gamma_{\alpha}$ fixed by the model (the
   model may rescale a component by a nonzero constant, which changes
   $\gamma_{\alpha}$ and the component but not its zero set);

subject to the two hypotheses

4. **nonempty admissible locus:** the **constraint locus**
   $$\Sigma:=\bigl\{(t,x)\in O:\ G(t,x)=0\bigr\}$$
   is nonempty and contained in $I_{0}\times Q$: every constrained
   configuration is an admissible configuration of the force-branch model and
   every constrained time lies in its time window;
5. **regularity:** for every $(t,x)\in\Sigma$ the Jacobian $D_{x}G(t,x)$
   ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]) is surjective, equivalently has rank
   $k$.

For $t\in\mathbb R$ write $\Sigma_{t}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{3N}:(t,x)\in\Sigma\}$
for the **instantaneous constraint locus**. Here a **$C^{2}$ embedded
submanifold of dimension $d$** in $\mathbb R^{n}$ means a subset $S$, with
its inherited topology, such that each $p\in S$ has an open neighbourhood
$U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ and a $C^{2}$ diffeomorphism
$h:U\to W$ onto an open $W\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ satisfying
$h(S\cap U)=W\cap(\mathbb R^{d}\times\{0\})$; both $h$ and its inverse
are $C^{2}$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].
This is the finite-regularity slice convention used for these loci;
[[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]] instead requires smooth charts.

Each nonempty $\Sigma_t$ is a $C^{2}$ embedded submanifold of dimension
$3N-k$. Indeed, at any $p\in\Sigma_t$ choose $k$ spatial columns of
$D_xG(t,p)$ giving an invertible minor, and permute coordinates as
$x=(u,v)\in\mathbb R^{3N-k}\times\mathbb R^k$. The fixed-time map
$H(u,v):=G(t,(u,v))$ is $C^2$ on the open slice of $O$, vanishes at $p$,
and has invertible $D_vH(p)$. Apply
[[thm-parametrized-implicit-function-theorem-with-higher-regularity]] with
regularity order $2$ and no parameter block: on open neighbourhoods
$P\times Q$ of $p$, its zero set is exactly $v=\varphi(u)$ for a
$C^2$ map $\varphi:P\to Q$. The map
$h(u,v)=(u,v-\varphi(u))$ is a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto the open set
$W=\{(u,w):u\in P,\ w+\varphi(u)\in Q\}$, with inverse
$(u,w)\mapsto(u,w+\varphi(u))$, and sends that graph to
$W\cap(\mathbb R^{3N-k}\times\{0\})$. This proves the claimed local
slice property. If $G$ is smooth, the smooth regular-value terminology of
[[def-regular-and-critical-points-and-values]] and the smooth conclusion of
[[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] also apply.
When $k=3N-1$ the instantaneous locus is locally a $C^2$ curve, and the number
$$\dim\Sigma_{t}=3N-k$$
is the **instantaneous degrees of freedom** of the constrained branch. The
set $V(t,x):=\ker D_{x}G(t,x)\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ has dimension $3N-k$ by
the rank-nullity theorem for matrices ([[cor-matrix-rank-nullity]]) and is called the space of **virtual displacements** of the datum
at $(t,x)$; its elements are the first-order differences of constrained
configurations at fixed time, in the sense of the mathematical definition
[[def-cm-holonomic-constraint-and-ideal-reactions]]. A vector
$v\in\mathbb R^{3N}$ is a **permitted velocity** at $(t,x)\in O$ when
$$G_{t}(t,x)+D_{x}G(t,x)\,v=0 .$$

**(b) Constrained curve families.** Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]). A **constrained curve family** of the
datum is a map $x:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ of class $C^{2}$ with
$(t,x(t))\in O$ and $G(t,x(t))=0$ for every $t\in J$; writing
$x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})$ with coordinate curves $x_{i}:J\to\mathbb R^{3}$ and
$w_{i}:=x_{i}'$, the componentwise derivatives of
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]] ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]];
$w_{i}$ is the coordinate velocity of label $i$), the chain rule
([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) applied to $t\mapsto G(t,x(t))$
gives
$$G_{t}\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+D_{x}G\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\,w(t)=0\qquad(t\in J),$$
so the velocity of a $C^{1}$ constrained curve family is permitted at every
time. A tuple $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})\in O\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ is **consistent
data** of the datum when $G(t_{0},x_{0})=0$ and
$G_{t}(t_{0},x_{0})+D_{x}G(t_{0},x_{0})v_{0}=0$; these are the initial data at
which constrained motions are posed below.

**(c) Reaction field and the constrained equation.** A **reaction field along
a curve family** $x:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ is a continuous map
$R:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$, of force dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$ in each
component. The **equation of the constrained datum along $x$** is
$$\mathsf M\,x''(t)=F\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr)+R(t)\qquad(t\in J),$$
componentwise $m_{i}x_{i}''(t)=F_{i}(t,x(t),w(t))+R_{i}(t)$. A
**holonomic-constraint model** consists of the force-branch data, a
holonomic-constraint datum $(O,k,G)$, and the declaration that the position
tuple of the labels satisfies $G(t,x(t))=0$ for all times while a reaction
field acts: a **constrained motion** of the model (with reaction $R$) is a
constrained curve family $x:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ together with a reaction field
$R$ satisfying the displayed equation. The force map $F$ is the model's
declared interaction force of the force branch, and $R$ is the additional
force contribution exerted by the mechanism that realizes the constraint; the
total force along a constrained motion is the pointwise sum $F+R$ in the sense
of clause (v) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]], read along the curve. The
reaction is **not** part of the force map: the constrained branch is the branch
excluded by clause (i) of that postulate, and the equation above is the
adopted equation of the constrained model. For any specified constrained curve
family $x$, this equation fixes the reaction uniquely as the residual field
$$R(t)=\mathsf Mx''(t)-F\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr).$$
Without an additional reaction law, the constraint and this equation do not
select which constrained curve families are dynamically admissible: every
$C^{2}$ constrained curve can be paired with its continuous residual field to
satisfy the equation. The ideal-reaction law of the postulate of this page is
the additional model assumption that selects among these candidates by
requiring the reaction to annihilate the virtual displacements.

**(d) Scleronomic and rheonomic constraints.** The datum is **scleronomic**
when the constraint locus is time-independent, in the precise sense that there
is a set $N\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ with
$$\Sigma=\bigl\{(t,x)\in O:\ x\in N\bigr\};$$
equivalently, membership in the locus is a condition on $x$ alone within $O$:
if $(t,x)\in\Sigma$ and $(t',x)\in O$, then $(t',x)\in\Sigma$ (the two
formulations are exchanged by passing between $N$ and the projection of
$\Sigma$ to $\mathbb R^{3N}$). For the standard product ambient set
$O=I_{0}\times Q$ the condition reads $\Sigma=I_{0}\times(N\cap Q)$. The datum
is **rheonomic** otherwise.

If the datum is scleronomic, then the declared presentation $G$, and every
$C^{2}$ presentation of the same locus with the rank hypothesis, satisfy
$$G_{t}(t,x)=0\qquad\text{for every }(t,x)\in\Sigma,$$
because for $x\in N$ every $(t,x)\in O$ lies in $\Sigma$, so $t\mapsto G(t,x)$
vanishes identically on the open set of times $\{t:(t,x)\in O\}$; this is the
form in which the classification is used by the balance theorems of this page.

The identity is a consequence of time-independence and **not** a criterion for
it. Write $s(x):=(x_{1})_{1}\in\mathbb R$ for the first Cartesian
component of particle $1$, of length dimension $\ell$, and fix a nonzero
speed $u$ of dimension $\ell\tau^{-1}$. The scalar presentation
$G(t,x):=(s(x)-ut)^{2}$, of dimension $\ell^{2}$, on
$O=\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ has the moving zero set $\{s(x)=ut\}$ while
$G_{t}(t,x)=-2u(s(x)-ut)$ vanishes at every point of that set; this presentation
violates the rank hypothesis, but the identity can also hold for a
rank-regular presentation: on
$O=\bigl((0,T_{*})\cup(2T_{*},3T_{*})\bigr)\times\mathbb R^{3N}$,
with $T_{*}>0$ of time dimension, the scalar $C^{2}$ map equal to
$s(x)$ on $(0,T_{*})\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and to a fixed
$L_{*}>0$ of length dimension on $(2T_{*},3T_{*})\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
has dimension $\ell$ and the rank-$1$ zero set
$\Sigma=(0,T_{*})\times\{x\in\mathbb R^{3N}:s(x)=0\}$ with $G_{t}=0$ on $\Sigma$,
yet $\Sigma$ is not of the form $\{(t,x)\in O:x\in N\}$ for any $N$: the point
$(T_{*}/2,0)\in\Sigma$ would force $0\in N$, and then $(5T_{*}/2,0)\in O$ would lie in
$\Sigma$. Hence the classification is a property of the locus, and the
identity is used only in the direction proved above.

Under a nowhere-vanishing $C^{2}$ rescaling $G'=\rho G$ one has
$D_{x}G'=\rho\,D_{x}G$ and $G'_{t}=\rho_{t}G+\rho G_{t}=\rho G_{t}$ at the
points of $\Sigma$, so the virtual displacements and permitted velocities are
unchanged, the multiplier of a motion transforms as
$\lambda'=\rho^{-1}\lambda$, and the reaction $D_{x}G'^{\mathsf T}\lambda'$
and the product $-\lambda'\cdot G'_{t}=-\lambda\cdot G_{t}$ of the rheonomic
power theorem are unchanged at the locus.

**(e) Status.** This item defines a model class: it fixes the constraint
datum, the constrained curves, the virtual displacements, the reaction field
and the equation of the constrained branch. It adopts no ideal-reaction law
(that is the content of the ideal-reaction postulate of this page), no particular force
law, and no measured value. Whether a concrete apparatus — a frictionless
joint, a smooth track, a taut rod or string, a no-slip contact — is described
by a holonomic-constraint model is an application-level judgement recorded with
the apparatus, together with the regime in which the rigidity, frictionlessness
or contact assumptions are adequate; the framework itself attaches no empirical
claim to the class.

The item declares a model class; it adopts no ideal-reaction law, no force law beyond the force branch and no measured value, and it does not assert that any real mechanism is described by the class.

items.title: Adopted ideal-reaction law for holonomic constraints: the d'Alembert condition, its scope and its limits
items.statement:
Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, in the setting of
[[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]]:

**(i) The ideal-reaction law.** Along every constrained motion $x:J\to
\mathbb R^{3N}$ of a holonomic-constraint model, with reaction field
$R:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$, the reaction annihilates every virtual displacement:

$$R(t)\cdot\delta=0\qquad\text{for every }t\in J\text{ and every }\delta\in V\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)=\ker D_{x}G\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr),$$

the pairing being the Euclidean inner product of $\mathbb R^{3N}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). This is the **d'Alembert condition** (the
condition of zero virtual work of the reaction) in the sense of
[[def-cm-holonomic-constraint-and-ideal-reactions]]. By the multiplier lemma
[[lem-cm-constraint-multipliers-and-accelerations]], applied at each time with
the surjective Jacobian $D_{x}G(t,x(t))$, the condition holds at time $t$ if
and only if there is a unique $\lambda(t)\in\mathbb R^{k}$ with
$$R(t)=D_{x}G\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\lambda(t);$$
this representation is a mathematical consequence of the condition and the
rank hypothesis, not a separate assumption, and the multiplier has dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}/\gamma_{\alpha}$ in component $\alpha$
([[def-cm01-units]]). The condition is imposed only along the motions of the
model, and it does not by itself determine $R$: it constrains $R$ at each time
to the $k$-dimensional conormal space, and which element occurs is fixed by
the twice-differentiated constraint through the balance theorem of this page.

**(ii) What is adopted.** Clause (i) is an adopted restriction on the
mechanism that realizes the constraint, not a theorem about bodies, tracks or
contacts. It is the idealization of a mechanism that exerts only the reaction
needed to maintain the constraint, distributed normally to the admissible
directions at each instant; the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] excludes constraint reactions from its force
maps, and this postulate is the additional law that closes the constrained
branch.

**(iii) Intended model identifications.** The framework intends clause (i) to
model, subject to the qualifications of clause (iv): frictionless hinges and
joints; smooth bilateral contacts and tracks; a taut light rod, and a taut
string while it stays taut; and no-slip rolling in the planar holonomic case,
provided the contact can supply the required tangential reaction. Each of
these identifications is an application-level statement made and recorded with
the apparatus; the framework asserts no measurement, no material parameter and
no numerical value here.

**(iv) Limits of the idealization.** The law is **not** asserted for:

1. constraints with dry sliding friction along an admissible direction, whose
   force has a component doing virtual work on admissible displacements — such
   friction must be declared as a separate force contribution with its own
   model;
2. unilateral contacts and mechanisms that can release the constraint (a bead
   on the outside of a surface, a string that can go slack, a block that can
   separate), which are maintained only while the required reaction satisfies
   a one-sided capability condition; where the condition fails, the constraint
   is released and a contact-change model is required, and none is supplied
   here;
3. points where the Jacobian $D_{x}G$ drops rank, which lie outside the
   regularity hypothesis of the datum and outside the representation above;
4. direct active forces on the modelled labels with a component along an
   admissible virtual displacement: these must be declared as additional
   force contributions. Prescribed motion of a support is instead encoded
   in the time-dependent constraint $G$ and is compatible with clause (i);
   its ideal reaction may do actual work as in clause (v). The dynamics and
   energy budget of equipment driving that support are not modelled here;
5. any claim that the mechanism can mechanically supply the computed
   reaction: the law computes the reaction the ideal constraint exerts; whether
   a physical contact, rod or string can supply it (friction cone, sign of a
   tensile force, strength limits, no-slip conditions) is an additional
   premise of an application.

**(v) The law is not a work statement.** Clause (i) concerns virtual
displacements at fixed time; it does not assert that the reaction performs no
work along the motion. For a scleronomic constraint the reaction power
vanishes identically, but for a rheonomic constraint the reaction can do work,
with $R\cdot x'=-\lambda\cdot G_{t}$; the precise statement, its static case
and worked models are the content of the rheonomic-power theorem and the
companion examples of this page.

**(vi) Status and empirical content.** The clause is adopted, not deduced; the
sources record the ideal-reaction condition as an additional physical
hypothesis attached to a constraint, not as a consequence of writing the
constraint down. The passage from clause (i) to the constrained equation of
motion is a theorem with explicit regularity hypotheses, proved on this page.
Whether the idealization is adequate for a given apparatus is decided by
comparing the model's conditional predictions with reported observations under
the stated regime, with the qualifications of clause (iv) carried along;
agreement of such a comparison is evidence about the combined model and
apparatus, not a proof of the idealization.
items.strategy: An adopted postulate: along every constrained motion the reaction annihilates every virtual displacement at fixed time, equivalently it is a transpose multiple of the constraint Jacobian by the multiplier lemma; the item records the intended model identifications, the exclusions (sliding friction, unilateral and contact-change mechanisms, rank loss, active drives, mechanical capability of the reaction) and the fact that the virtual-work condition is not a statement about actual work, conservation or measured values.

items.title: Ideal holonomic constraints determine the reaction: multiplier form, explicit acceleration, unique constrained motions and the reaction-power identity
items.statement:
Adopt a holonomic-constraint model of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]]
with datum $(O,k,G)$, mass operator $\mathsf M$, force map $F$, and the
ideal-reaction law of [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. Suppose, in addition
to the hypotheses of those items:

**(h1)** $G$ is of class $C^{3}$ on $O$, and $D_{x}G(t,x)$ has rank $k$ for
every $(t,x)\in O$ (not only on the constraint locus);

**(h2)** the force map is of class $C^{1}$ on
$I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

Set $O':=O\cap(I_{0}\times Q)$. This is an open nonempty set because
$\Sigma\subseteq O'$ and $\Sigma$ is nonempty. The matrix-valued map
$C:O\to M_{k}(\mathbb R)$ below is defined on $O$, while
$\Lambda:O'\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\to\mathbb R^{k}$ and
$a:O'\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ are defined on the
force-map domain restricted to the constraint datum; this is the time-state
domain of the first-order system. Every constrained motion in the statement has
$(t,x(t))\in\Sigma\subseteq O'$, so these functions are defined along it.

Let $x:J\to Q$ be a constrained motion of the model with reaction field $R$
satisfying the ideal-reaction law, on an interval $J\subseteq I_{0}$ with
nonempty interior, and write $w=x'$ for its velocity. Then:

1. **multiplier form.** For every $t\in J$ there is a unique
   $\lambda(t)\in\mathbb R^{k}$ with $R(t)=D_{x}G(t,x(t))^{\mathsf T}\lambda(t)$;
   the map $\lambda:J\to\mathbb R^{k}$ so defined is continuous, and with

$$C(t,x):=D_{x}G(t,x)\,\mathsf M^{-1}D_{x}G(t,x)^{\mathsf T},\qquad \Lambda(t,x,v):=-C(t,x)^{-1}\Bigl[D_{x}G\,\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)+G_{tt}+2G_{tq}[v]+G_{qq}[v,v]\Bigr],$$

   the terms being evaluated at $(t,x)$ or $(t,x,v)$, the $k\times k$ matrix
   $C(t,x)$ is symmetric positive definite and invertible and
   $$\lambda(t)=\Lambda\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J):$$
   the multiplier, and hence the reaction, is determined by the model data
   and the motion, not a free or measured quantity.

2. **determined dynamics.** With
   $a(t,x,v):=\mathsf M^{-1}\bigl(F(t,x,v)+D_{x}G(t,x)^{\mathsf T}\Lambda(t,x,v)\bigr)$,
   the tuple $(x,w)$ solves the first-order system
   $$x'=v,\qquad v'=a(t,x,v)$$
   on $J$; conversely every solution $(x,v)$ of this system on an interval
   whose initial datum is consistent, with
   $R(t):=D_{x}G(t,x(t))^{\mathsf T}\Lambda(t,x(t),v(t))$, is a constrained
   motion of the model satisfying the ideal-reaction law; and through every
   consistent datum $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})$ there is a unique maximal solution
   of the system. Hence the holonomic-constraint model with ideal reactions
   has determined dynamics on its constraint locus.

3. **preservation.** Along every solution of clause 2 with consistent data,
   $$G\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)=0,\qquad G_{t}\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+D_{x}G\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)v(t)=0$$
   for every $t$ of its maximal interval.

4. **reaction power.** Along every ideal constrained motion as in clause 1,
   $$R(t)\cdot w(t)=-\lambda(t)\cdot G_{t}\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J),$$
   the pairings being the Euclidean inner products.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and ideal-reaction
law and on hypotheses (h1)-(h2); it asserts no empirical value, and the
multiplier is a representation tied to the declared components of $G$.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: identify the model data with the mathematical regular-holonomic constraint chart, use the multiplier lemma for the conormal representation of the ideal reaction and the chart proposition for regularity, existence, uniqueness and preservation; differentiate the constraint twice along the motion to evaluate the multiplier explicitly, and derive the reaction-power identity R dot x' = -lambda G_t.
items.physical_scope: The conditional dynamics of a holonomic-constraint model with the adopted ideal-reaction law: the reaction is the transpose multiple of the constraint Jacobian with a unique continuous multiplier, the multiplier and the constrained acceleration are the explicit functions Lambda and a of the datum, the constrained motions with permitted velocity are exactly the solutions of the resulting first-order system with consistent data, the constraint and its differentiated form are preserved, and the reaction power equals minus the multiplier paired with the time derivative of the constraint. Empirical qualifications of the idealization and the exclusions of the postulate are carried; no measured value and no energy-conservation claim is asserted.

items.title: Reaction work and mechanical-energy balance for ideal holonomic constraints: vanishing power for scleronomic constraints and the rheonomic work term
items.statement:
Adopt a holonomic-constraint model of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]]
with datum $(O,k,G)$ and the ideal-reaction law of
[[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. Suppose, in addition to the model
hypotheses, that $G$ is of class $C^{3}$ on $O$ and $D_{x}G(t,x)$ has rank
$k$ for every $(t,x)\in O$, and that the force map is of class $C^{1}$ on
$I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$; these are hypotheses (h1)-(h2) of
[[pthm-cm06-multiplier-balance]]. Let
$x:J\to Q$ be a constrained motion with ideal reaction $R$ on an interval
$J\subseteq I_{0}$ with nonempty interior, with velocity $w=x'$ and multiplier
$\lambda:J\to\mathbb R^{k}$ as in [[pthm-cm06-multiplier-balance]] clause 1.
Suppose further that the model's force map is presented through a potential
with residual forces in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]: a $C^{2}$ function
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and maps
$d_{i}:I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ with the
standing regularity of clause (iii) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]], such
that
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N)$$
on the state domain ([[def-cm01-units]] for the dimensions). Write
$K$ and $E(t):=K(t)+U(t,x(t))$ for the kinetic and mechanical energy of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]] clauses (b),(d) and of clause (b) of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], and
$\mathfrak d_{i}(t):=d_{i}(t,x(t),w(t))$ for the evaluated residual forces.
Then:

1. **reaction power and reaction work.** For every $t\in J$,
   $$R(t)\cdot w(t)=-\lambda(t)\cdot G_{t}\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr),$$
   and for all $t_{0}<t_{1}$ in $J$, $\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}R(t)\cdot w(t)\,dt
   =-\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\lambda(t)\cdot G_{t}(t,x(t))\,dt$. If the datum is
   scleronomic, then $R\cdot w\equiv0$ on $J$ and the reaction performs no
   work over any subinterval.

2. **mechanical-energy balance.** $E$ is differentiable on $J$ and
   $$E'(t)=\partial_{t}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+\sum_{i}\bigl\langle\mathfrak d_{i}(t),w_{i}(t)\bigr\rangle-\lambda(t)\cdot G_{t}\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J):$$
   the mechanical energy changes at the rate of the explicit time dependence
   of the potential, the power of the residual forces, and the constraint
   term $-\lambda\cdot G_{t}$, which vanishes identically for a scleronomic
   constraint.

3. **conservation in the static scleronomic case.** If the datum is
   scleronomic, $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ on $I_{0}\times Q$, and
   $\mathfrak d_{i}\equiv0$ for every $i$ along the motion, then $E$ is
   constant on $J$.

4. **integrated work form.** For all $t_{0}<t_{1}$ in $J$,
   $$K(t_{1})-K(t_{0})=U\bigl(t_{0},x(t_{0})\bigr)-U\bigl(t_{1},x(t_{1})\bigr)+\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\Bigl[\partial_{t}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+\sum_{i}\bigl\langle\mathfrak d_{i}(t),w_{i}(t)\bigr\rangle-\lambda(t)\cdot G_{t}\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\Bigr]dt .$$

The constraint term of clause 2 is not a force of the model's force map: it is
the mechanical work performed by the ideal mechanism that maintains a
time-dependent constraint, and clause 1 records that this work is exactly the
virtual-work-free reaction's actual power. The statement is conditional on the
adopted model, idealization and potential presentation; it asserts no measured
value.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: compute the reaction power from the multiplier representation and the differentiated constraint, then apply the mathematical work-energy balance with the total non-potential force (residual plus reaction); read off the vanishing of the reaction work for scleronomic constraints, the rheonomic work term, the conservation case and the integrated work form.
items.physical_scope: The work and energy statements of an ideal holonomic-constraint model with an ambient force map presented through a potential with residual forces: the reaction power equals minus the multiplier paired with the time derivative of the constraint, so scleronomic ideal constraints perform no work, while rheonomic ideal constraints can change the mechanical energy through a term that is not a residual force of the model; the mechanical-energy balance carries that term, a scleronomic constraint with a static potential and vanishing residual forces along the motion is sufficient for conservation, and the integrated work form is stated. These sufficient conditions are not necessary: conservation holds along a motion exactly when the total energy-rate expression vanishes there. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted model and idealization, with the empirical qualifications of the ideal-reaction postulate carried; no measured value is asserted.

items.title: Moving spatial charts of an inertial frame: rotating and translating coordinates, angular velocity and inertial terms
items.statement:
Fix one inertial frame $F=\bigl(o,u,(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})\bigr)$ of the model with
adapted coordinates $(t,x)$ ([[post-cm01-frames]]); lengths and times are read
in metres and seconds ([[def-cm01-units]]). A **moving spatial chart** of this
frame is the following kinematic data:

**(a) Data.** A nondegenerate interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$
([[def-interval]]) together with maps
$$c:I\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3},\qquad R:I\longrightarrow SO(3),$$
the matrix $R(t)$ being identified with its nine entries, such that all
components of $c$ and all entries of $R$ have continuous second derivatives on
$I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]],
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]); we then say that $c$ and $R$
are of class $C^{2}$. The components $c_j(t)$ are spatial coordinates, with
$[c_j]=\ell$, and the entries of $R(t)$ are dimensionless, with
$[R_{ij}]=1$; the moving coordinates $y_j$ also have dimension $\ell$
([[def-cm01-units]]). The map
$$\Phi:I\times\mathbb R^{3}\longrightarrow I\times\mathbb R^{3},\qquad \Phi(t,y):=\bigl(t,\,R(t)y+c(t)\bigr),$$
is the **coordinate change of the chart**: for $t\in I$ it identifies the
triple $y\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with the point of the inertial chart whose
coordinates are $x=R(t)y+c(t)$. The curve $t\mapsto c(t)$ is the **reference
curve** of the chart and the family $R(t)$ its **rotation**; the chart is
**attached to** the fixed inertial frame, and its data are kinematic data of
the description, not new physical objects.

**(b) Coordinate curves, velocities and accelerations.** Let $J\subseteq I$
be an interval with nonempty interior and let $x:J\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be a
curve of class $C^{2}$ in the inertial chart (for instance the coordinate
curve of a worldline in the sense of [[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]). The
**coordinate curve of $x$ in the moving chart** is
$$y(t):=R(t)^{\mathsf T}\bigl(x(t)-c(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J);$$
its **coordinate velocity** and **coordinate acceleration in the moving
chart** are the componentwise derivatives $\dot y:=y'$ and $\ddot y:=y''$
([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), of dimensions
$\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $\ell\tau^{-2}$. These are chart-local notions: because
the chart is generally time-dependent, these need not be the coordinate
velocity and acceleration of an inertial frame. If $R$ is constant and $c$ is
affine on $I$, they agree on $I$ with the corresponding quantities in the
inertial frame whose adapted chart restricts to this chart. Their relation to
the fixed frame $F$ is the kinematic identity of the cited mathematical
supplier, not an identification with the quantities read in $F$.

**(c) Angular velocity of the chart.** Put $\Omega(t):=R(t)^{\mathsf T}R'(t)$.
By [[lem-cm-moving-frame-acceleration-identity]] clause 1, $\Omega(t)$ is
skew-symmetric for every $t$, and by clause 2 there is a unique
$\omega(t)\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$\Omega(t)z=\omega(t)\times z\qquad(z\in\mathbb R^{3}),$$
the cross product being that of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. The vector
$\omega(t)$ is the **angular velocity of the chart** in the convention
$\Omega=R^{\mathsf T}R'$ (the **body convention**), of dimension
$\tau^{-1}$ read in radians per second; its components are read off the three
entries of $\Omega$ above the diagonal. With the opposite convention
$\Omega_{s}:=R'R^{\mathsf T}$ one has
$\Omega_{s}=R\,\Omega\,R^{\mathsf T}=[R\omega]_{\times}$ by clause 3 of
[[lem-cm-skew-matrix-cross-product-correspondence]] and
[[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]], so the representing vector of the
opposite convention is $R(t)\omega(t)$: the two conventions differ by the
rotation, and every statement of this framework names the one it uses. This
definition uses the body convention throughout.

**(d) Inertial terms.** For $(t,y,\dot y)\in I\times\mathbb R^{3}\times\mathbb R^{3}$
define
$$\tau(t,y,\dot y):=-\Bigl(2\,\omega(t)\times\dot y+\omega'(t)\times y+\omega(t)\times\bigl(\omega(t)\times y\bigr)+R(t)^{\mathsf T}c''(t)\Bigr),$$
of dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$; $\tau$ is the field of **inertial terms** of the
chart, per unit mass in the sense that the moving-chart equation of the next
item carries the factor $m\tau$ for a label of mass $m$. Its four additive
contributions are named, in order: the **Coriolis term** $-2\omega\times\dot y$,
the **Euler term** $-\omega'\times y$, the **centrifugal term**
$-\omega\times(\omega\times y)$, and the **translational term**
$-R^{\mathsf T}c''$. The names are conventions attached to the displayed
terms; the definition attaches no force to them, and clause (f) records their
kinematic status.

**(e) Curves at rest in the chart.** For fixed $y_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ let
$x_{y_{0}}(s):=R(s)y_{0}+c(s)$ be the spatial coordinate curve in the inertial
chart. Its spacetime lift is the curve $\gamma_{y_{0}}:I\to A$ defined by
$$\gamma_{y_{0}}(s):=o+su+\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(x_{y_{0}}(s)\bigr)_{j}e_{j}.$$
It is $C^{2}$ and satisfies $t(\gamma_{y_{0}}(s))=s$, so it has the
parameter condition of [[post-cm01-worldlines]]. This lifted curve is the path
of a point **at rest in the chart**; whether it is assigned as the worldline of
a particle label is a separate declaration of a model and is not made here.

**(f) Status.** A moving chart is a time-dependent coordinate description
attached to one inertial frame. In general it is not an inertial frame of the
model: [[post-cm01-frames]] defines inertial charts using a fixed spatial basis
and an affine reference curve. When $R$ is constant and $c$ is affine on $I$,
the coordinate change has the form of an allowed Galilean frame change and is
the restriction to $I$ of an adapted chart. The inertial-forces theorem of
this page proves that these are exactly the data for which the inertial terms
of clause (d) vanish identically. A moving chart is not an observer
congruence: a congruence is a family of curves of the spacetime data, whereas
a chart is a coordinate map. The identity
relating the inertial-chart acceleration to the moving-chart acceleration of
the same curve is the mathematical lemma cited in clause (c); the equation of
motion of a force model in the moving chart, with the inertial terms entering
as the mass multiples $m\tau$, is the inertial-forces theorem of this page,
with its own hypotheses. Nothing in this definition asserts a force law, an
equation of motion, a transformation law for physical interactions or a
measured value.
items.strategy: A kinematic definition: it fixes the moving spatial chart of a fixed inertial frame by a C^2 reference curve and rotation, the coordinate curves, velocities and accelerations read in the chart, the angular velocity in the stated body convention with the conversion to the opposite convention, the four inertial terms, the curves at rest in the chart, and the status of the object as a coordinate description rather than an inertial frame or an observer congruence; no force law or measured value.
items.physical_scope: Definition of the moving spatial charts of the Newtonian model: a translating and rotating coordinate description attached to a fixed inertial frame, its reference curve and rotation, the coordinate curves, velocities and accelerations read in it, the angular velocity of the chart in a stated convention, and the four inertial terms. In general the moving chart is not an inertial frame; when its rotation is constant and its reference curve is affine, its restriction is an adapted chart of another inertial frame. A chart is not an observer congruence. The item asserts no force law, no equation of motion and no measured value.

items.title: The equation of motion in a moving chart: inertial terms, inertial forces, and when it restricts to an inertial chart
items.statement:
Adopt the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$ labels
with masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, time window $I_{0}$, open configuration
domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ and force map $F$ with the standing
regularity; fix one inertial frame $F$ with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$
([[post-cm01-frames]], [[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Let a moving spatial chart of $F$ be given by data
$(I,c,R)$ with $I\subseteq I_{0}$ ([[def-cm06-moving-frame]]), with angular
velocity $\omega$ and inertial-terms field
$$\tau(t,y,\dot y):=-\Bigl(2\,\omega(t)\times\dot y+\omega'(t)\times y+\omega(t)\times\bigl(\omega(t)\times y\bigr)+R(t)^{\mathsf T}c''(t)\Bigr).$$

Let $x:J\to Q$ be a **motion** of the model on an interval $J\subseteq I$ with
nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] clause (c)):
$$m_{i}x_{i}''(t)=F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J),$$
with $w=x'$ the coordinate velocity of the labels, and for each label define
the moving-chart coordinate curve and its derivatives
$$y_{i}(t):=R(t)^{\mathsf T}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-c(t)\bigr),\qquad \dot y_{i}=y_{i}',\qquad \ddot y_{i}=y_{i}''.$$
Then:

1. **moving-chart equation.** For every $i$ and every $t\in J$,
   $$m_{i}\,\ddot y_{i}(t)=R(t)^{\mathsf T}F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr)+m_{i}\,\tau\bigl(t,y_{i}(t),\dot y_{i}(t)\bigr).$$

2. **inertial forces.** Define the **inertial force** on label $i$ along the
   motion by $F_{i}^{\mathrm{in}}(t):=m_{i}\tau(t,y_{i}(t),\dot y_{i}(t))$,
   with the four additive components $-2m_{i}\omega\times\dot y_{i}$,
   $-m_{i}\omega'\times y_{i}$, $-m_{i}\omega\times(\omega\times y_{i})$ and
   $-m_{i}R^{\mathsf T}c''$ (Coriolis, Euler, centrifugal and translational).
   Then clause 1 reads $m_{i}\ddot y_{i}=R^{\mathsf T}F_{i}+F_{i}^{\mathrm{in}}$.
   The inertial forces are determined by the chart's motion and the label's
   mass; they are **not** contributions of the model's force map $F$, and
   a general moving chart is not an inertial frame of the model; clause 3
   characterizes the case in which it is the restriction of another inertial
   chart.

3. **criterion for an inertial chart.** The inertial terms vanish
   identically, $\tau(t,y,\dot y)=0$ for every $(t,y,\dot y)\in I\times\mathbb R^{3}\times\mathbb R^{3}$,
   if and only if $R$ is constant on $I$ and $c$ is affine on $I$. In that
   case the moving chart $(t,y)$ on $I$ is the restriction of the adapted
   coordinate chart of an inertial frame $F_{*}$ of the model related to $F$ by a Galilean
   transformation with vanishing time shift, and clause 1 reduces for each
   label to $m_{i}\ddot y_{i}=R^{\mathsf T}F_{i}(t,x(t),w(t))$, which is the
   transformed equation of motion of clause (vi) of
   [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] read in $F_{*}$. Conversely, if the
   moving chart on $I$ is the restriction of the adapted chart of an inertial frame related to $F$ by a
   Galilean transformation with vanishing time shift, then $R$ is constant
   and $c$ is affine and $\tau\equiv0$.

The identity of clause 1 is a conditional consequence of the adopted force
branch and of the chart's kinematics; clause 3 is its consistency check
against the frame class of [[post-cm01-frames]]. No claim is made that a
moving chart is physically equivalent to an inertial frame with an additional
force field, and no measured value is asserted.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: apply the mathematical rotating-frame acceleration identity to each label of a motion of the force model and read off the inertial terms and their mass multiples; characterize the vanishing of the inertial terms by a short computation as exactly the charts with constant rotation and affine reference curve, and identify those charts as the adapted charts of inertial frames, recovering the force-covariance law.
items.physical_scope: The conditional description of the motions of a force-branch model in a rigidly moving and rotating spatial chart: the exact identity for the coordinate acceleration with the four inertial terms, the reading of those terms as mass-proportional inertial forces, and the characterization of exactly inertial charts as the charts whose inertial terms vanish, in which case the framework's force-covariance law is recovered. The inertial terms are properties of the chart's motion, not forces of the model's force map; the item asserts no equivalence between a moving chart and a gravitational field, and no measured value.

items.title: Velocity-constraint (nonholonomic) models of the force branch: constant-rank constraint laws, the d'Alembert reaction and holonomic equivalence
items.statement:
Adopt the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$ labels
with masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, a nondegenerate open time window
$I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$, an open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$
and a force map $F$ with the standing regularity
([[def-cm01-configuration]], [[def-cm01-units]]). Fix one inertial frame with
adapted coordinates $(t,x)$ and write $x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})\in\mathbb R^{3N}$
with coordinate velocity $w=x'$ ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]],
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]).

**(a) Velocity-constraint datum.** A **velocity-constraint datum** on this
data is a quadruple $(O_{v},k',A,b)$ with:

1. an **ambient set** $O_{v}\subseteq I_{0}\times Q$, open and nonempty;
2. an integer $k'$ with $1\le k'\le 3N-1$;
3. maps $A:O_{v}\to M_{k'\times 3N}(\mathbb R)$ and
   $b:O_{v}\to\mathbb R^{k'}$ of class $C^{2}$
   ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), of declared dimensions
   chosen so that every row satisfies $[A_{\alpha j}w_{j}]=[b_{\alpha}]$ —
   the output of each row of the law below is a single declared quantity;
4. the **constant-rank hypothesis**: $A(t,x)$ has rank $k'$ for every
   $(t,x)\in O_{v}$, equivalently the linear map
   $A(t,x):\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{k'}$ is surjective
   ([[def-linear-map]], [[cor-matrix-rank-nullity]]).

The **constraint law** of the datum is
$$A(t,x)\,w+b(t,x)=0 .$$

**(b) Admissible velocities, virtual displacements, admissible curves.** For
$(t,x)\in O_{v}$ the **admissible velocities** are the vectors
$v\in\mathbb R^{3N}$ with $A(t,x)v+b(t,x)=0$. They form the nonempty affine
subspace $v_{0}+\ker A(t,x)$ (nonempty because $A(t,x)$ is surjective), with
direction the linear space
$$V(t,x):=\ker A(t,x)\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \dim V(t,x)=3N-k'$$
by rank-nullity ([[cor-matrix-rank-nullity]]). The elements of $V(t,x)$ are
the **virtual displacements** of the datum at $(t,x)$: the admissible
velocity differences at frozen time and configuration, in the Chetaev
prescription of [[def-cm-nonholonomic-velocity-constraint-law]]. A
**kinematically admissible curve family** is a map $x:J\to Q$ of class $C^{2}$
on an interval $J\subseteq I_{0}$ with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]])
such that $(t,x(t))\in O_{v}$ and
$A(t,x(t))x'(t)+b(t,x(t))=0$ for every $t\in J$; its velocity at each time is
admissible by definition.

**(c) d'Alembert velocity-constraint model.** A **velocity-constraint model**
consists of the force-branch data, a velocity-constraint datum $(O_{v},k',A,b)$
and the declaration that the labels' motion satisfies the constraint law
while a reaction field acts: a **motion** of the model is a kinematically
admissible curve family $x:J\to Q$ together with a continuous reaction field
$R:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ of force dimension satisfying
$$\mathsf M\,x''(t)=F\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)+R(t)\qquad(t\in J),$$
with $\mathsf M$ the mass operator of [[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (d).
The model is a **d'Alembert model** when, in addition, the reaction is
**ideal**: along every motion,
$$R(t)\cdot\delta=0\qquad\text{for every }\delta\in V\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)=\ker A\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr),$$
the pairing being the Euclidean inner product ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).
This is the **adopted idealization** of the mechanism that realizes the
velocity constraint — the analogue for velocity constraints of the ideal
reaction law of the holonomic branch — and it is not a consequence of the
constraint being imposed. By the multiplier lemma
([[lem-linear-functional-annihilating-kernel-of-a-surjection-is-a-transpose-multiple]]),
applied at each time to the surjective $A(t,x(t))$, the ideal condition holds
at time $t$ if and only if there is a unique $\mu(t)\in\mathbb R^{k'}$ with
$$R(t)=A\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\mu(t);$$
the representation is a mathematical consequence of the condition and the
rank hypothesis, while the ideal condition itself is the adopted part. The
equation of the d'Alembert model in multiplier form is therefore
$\mathsf Mx''=F+A^{\mathsf T}\mu$ along an ideal motion.

**(d) Holonomic equivalence and nonholonomic models.** The datum is
**holonomic-equivalent** on $O_{v}$ when there exist a $C^{2}$ map
$\Phi:O_{v}\to\mathbb R^{k'}$ with $\Phi_{x}$ of rank $k'$ on $O_{v}$ and a
$C^{2}$ map $\varrho:O_{v}\to GL(k',\mathbb R)$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]],
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]) with
$$A(t,x)=\varrho(t,x)\,\Phi_{x}(t,x),\qquad b(t,x)=\varrho(t,x)\,\Phi_{t}(t,x)\qquad\text{on }O_{v};$$
for a physical datum, each component $\Phi_{\beta}$ has a declared dimension
$\phi_{\beta}$. With $[x_j]=\ell$ and $[t]=\tau$, assign
$[\varrho_{\alpha\beta}]=[b_{\alpha}]\tau/\phi_{\beta}$; then every term
in the two matrix products has the declared dimension of the corresponding
entry of $A$ or $b$. These component assignments are part of the model's
declaration.
The datum is **locally holonomic-equivalent at a point** when such a pair exists on some open neighbourhood of that point, and **locally nonholonomic there** when no such neighbourhood and pair exists, as in [[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (e). A **nonholonomic model** in this local sense specifies a point (or region of points) with this failure. Absence of one pair on the whole domain $O_v$ alone is insufficient, since a global obstruction need not be local nonintegrability. In
the holonomic-equivalent case the law is the differentiated family of
position constraints $\Phi(t,x)=\text{constant}$: for a $C^{1}$ curve with
$(t,x(t))\in O_{v}$, the chain rule
([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) gives
$$\frac{d}{dt}\Phi\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)=\Phi_{t}+\Phi_{x}x'=\varrho^{-1}\bigl(b+Ax'\bigr),$$
so the constraint law holds exactly when $\Phi(t,x(t))$ is constant; a
holonomic-equivalent model is thus one whose constraint is equivalent to a
family of $k'$ independent position constraints with regular differentials,
presented through the nowhere-vanishing factor $\varrho$. For $k'=1$ the
factorization $A=\varrho\Phi_x$, $b=\varrho\Phi_t$ says that the one-form
$b\,dt+A\cdot dx$ is $\varrho\,d\Phi$: in this single-row case, local
nonholonomicity means that no such integrating factor and regular potential
exist on any neighbourhood of the specified point. For $k'>1$, local
nonholonomicity is defined by failure of the matrix factorization above, not
by a single one-form criterion. In a separate reduced two-coordinate model
$q=(s,\theta)\in\mathbb R^{2}$ of a disk rolling along a straight line (not
the $3N$-coordinate datum of clauses (a)-(c)), let $[s]=[a]=\ell$,
$[\theta]=1$ and $a>0$. Its no-slip law $s'-a\theta'=0$ is
holonomic-equivalent with $A=(1,-a)$, $b=0$,
$\Phi(s,\theta)=s-a\theta$ of dimension $\ell$, and dimensionless
$\varrho=1$; the velocity constraint $z'=xy'$ of
[[def-cm-nonholonomic-velocity-constraint-law]] is not: an integrating factor
would make the distribution $\ker A$ tangent to the level sets of $\Phi$, and
[[prop-cm-nonholonomic-distribution-is-not-tangent-to-level-sets]] proves
that this distribution is not tangent to the level sets of any $C^{2}$
function with nonvanishing differential. Tong's cited example is a specific
coin of radius $R>0$ rolling without slipping down a slope, with generalized
coordinates $(x,y,\theta,\phi)$ and velocity constraints
$$x'=R\phi'\sin\theta,\qquad y'=R\phi'\cos\theta,$$
where $x,y,R$ have length dimension and $\theta,\phi$ are angles in radians,
which he identifies as non-holonomic (Section 2.3.2, Eq. (2.41)). This is a
source-reported classification of that rolling-coin model; this item does not
prove it or classify all three-dimensional rolling models.

**(e) Status and scope.** The d'Alembert law of clause (c) is a prescription
for the reaction at frozen time and configuration, adopted as the physical
idealization of the mechanism; it is **not** identified with the vakonomic
(stationary augmented action) prescription of
[[def-cm-nonholonomic-velocity-constraint-law]]. For the sample model $z'=xy'$
with unit mass, zero applied force and initial data
$(x,y,z)(0)=(0,0,0)$, $(x',y',z')(0)=(1,1,0)$,
[[cex-cm-dalembert-and-vakonomic-evolutions-differ]] proves that there is a
unique maximal d'Alembert motion on $\mathbb R$ with those data. Every
other d'Alembert motion through the datum is its restriction; neither the
maximal motion nor any such restriction is vakonomic. Thus the d'Alembert
solution set is not a subset of the vakonomic solution set for that datum,
and the two sets are unequal; this does not assert that a vakonomic motion
with those data exists. The closing remark of this page records the
distinction and its scope. The framework excludes from
this branch: points where the rank of $A$ drops (the multiplier system
degenerates there, and no continuation is asserted); unilateral constraints
and contact changes (a skate leaving the ground, a wheel beginning to slip),
which require their own mode-change models; impacts; dry friction along
admissible directions, which must be declared as a separate force
contribution; and active drives, whose driving is an additional force of the
model. Whether a concrete mechanism is described by this class, and whether
its reaction can supply the computed multiplier, are application-level
statements recorded with the apparatus; the definition asserts no measured
value.

items.title: The d'Alembert and vakonomic prescriptions are different models: what is proved, what is adopted, and which questions are open
items.statement:
For a velocity-constraint datum $(O_{v},k',A,b)$ of
[[def-cm06-nonholonomic-model]] the framework's model is the **d'Alembert
model**: admissible curves satisfy $Ax'+b=0$, and the reaction is the ideal
(Chetaev) reaction, annihilating the frozen virtual displacements
$\ker A(t,x(t))$ at each instant, equivalently $R=A^{\mathsf T}\mu$ for a
unique multiplier. The **vakonomic** prescription of
[[def-cm-nonholonomic-velocity-constraint-law]] is a different construction:
one forms the augmented functional
$$\Phi(q,\eta)=\int_{a}^{b}\Bigl[\tfrac12|q'|^{2}+\eta\,(z'-xy')\Bigr]dt$$
for the sample constraint $z'=xy'$ and a multiplier function $\eta$, and asks
for pairs $(q,\eta)$ stationary under variations of both the curve and the
multiplier. The two prescriptions are definitions of two different laws for
the same constraint; neither is a theorem about the other, and the framework
adopts the d'Alembert one for its nonholonomic models.


For the constraint $z'=xy'$ with unit mass, zero applied force and initial
data $(x,y,z)(0)=(0,0,0)$, $(x',y',z')(0)=(1,1,0)$,
[[cex-cm-dalembert-and-vakonomic-evolutions-differ]] proves that the unique
maximal d'Alembert motion on $\mathbb R$ is not vakonomic. Every other
d'Alembert motion with these data is its restriction, and no such
restriction is vakonomic either. Thus the set of
d'Alembert motions with this initial datum is not a subset of the vakonomic
motions with the same datum, so the two solution sets are unequal; the
counterexample does not assert that a vakonomic motion with these data exists.
Its contradiction follows because the exhibited d'Alembert trajectory has
$x''=0$, which would force the vakonomic multiplier $\eta$ to vanish on an
interval and then force $y''=0$, contrary to its explicit formula. The same
constraint is genuinely nonholonomic in the sense of
clause (d) of [[def-cm06-nonholonomic-model]]:
[[prop-cm-nonholonomic-distribution-is-not-tangent-to-level-sets]] proves
that its distribution is not tangent to the level sets of any $C^{2}$ function
with nonvanishing differential. The conclusions are mathematical statements
about the two prescriptions; they are read into this page's model through the
definitions, with the model's status and exclusions of clause (e) carried
along.


The ideal (d'Alembert) condition for the holonomic branch is the adopted
postulate [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]], and the corresponding ideal
condition for velocity constraints is built into the definition of the
d'Alembert model. In particular, no variational principle is claimed for the
nonholonomic models of this page: inserting the velocity constraint into a
Lagrangian and varying without constraint is the vakonomic construction and
generally produces different equations, and substituting the constraint into
the kinetic energy of a constrained system is justified only in the
holonomic-equivalent case, where the substitution parametrizes the position
locus rather than imposing a velocity law. The sources record both warnings
(SICM §1.10.3; Stewart, printed page 25; Cline §§5.7 and 6.9; Cortes et al.).


The following are outside this page and remain open here: the behaviour of
either prescription at a point where the rank of $A$ drops; unilateral
constraints and contact-mode changes (a body that leaves a surface or begins
to slip), which require mode-change models with impact or friction laws; the
determination of which prescription describes a given physical mechanism; and
the quantitative comparison of either model with reported observations.
Rolling is a family of models rather than one model: the reduced planar
two-coordinate no-slip law used on the companion page is holonomic-equivalent, and the straight-rolling
exception is noted in the sources. Tong's cited example is the specific coin
of radius $R$ rolling without slipping down a slope, with coordinates
$(x,y,\theta,\phi)$ and constraints $x'=R\phi'\sin\theta$,
$y'=R\phi'\cos\theta$ (Section 2.3.2, Eq. (2.41)); it is reported there as
nonholonomic. This remark asserts no classification of all three-dimensional
rolling models and supplies no local proof for Tong's example. Friction,
rolling resistance, material deformation and the ability of a contact to
supply the required reaction are application-level premises; no measured
value and no empirical adequacy claim is made by any item of this page.
items.strategy: A scope remark: it distinguishes the d'Alembert (Chetaev) prescription adopted by the framework's nonholonomic models from the vakonomic stationary-augmented-action prescription, cites the proved discrepancy for the constraint z'=xy' and the non-integrability result, warns against silent constraint substitution, and records the open questions of rank and contact changes, rolling models and empirical adequacy without any measured value.
items.physical_scope: Scope remark distinguishing the two prescriptions for a velocity-constrained model: the d'Alembert (Chetaev, frozen-kernel) law adopted by this framework's nonholonomic models and the vakonomic (stationary augmented action) prescription, with the proved non-inclusion of the d'Alembert solution set in the vakonomic solution set for one specified z'=xy' initial datum, the exclusion of silent constraint substitution, and the open questions of rank and contact changes, rolling models and empirical adequacy. The remark asserts no measured value and no experimental comparison.

title: Regular constraints and moving frames — Examples

items.title: A bead on a uniformly rotating straight wire: the rheonomic ideal constraint, its reaction, and the work it performs
items.statement:
Declare a one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and force map
$$F:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3}\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3},\qquad F(t,\mathbf x,\mathbf v):=(0,\,0,\,-mg),$$
where $[m]=\mu$ and $g>0$ has dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$ (the uniform
downward field; conventions of [[def-cm01-units]]). Constrain the label,
without friction, to the straight wire through the origin that rotates in the
plane $z=0$ about the $z$-axis with constant angular speed $\Omega>0$, and to
that plane, by the regular holonomic-constraint datum
$$O:=\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3},\quad k:=2,\qquad G(t,x,y,z):=\bigl(-x\sin\Omega t+y\cos\Omega t,\ z\bigr)$$
of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]], and adopt the ideal-reaction law
of [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. Both components of $G$ have length
dimension $\ell$, and $[\Omega]=\tau^{-1}$.

Let $r_{0}>0$ be a length and $u_{0}\in\mathbb R$ the initial radial speed,
with $[r_{0}]=\ell$ and $[u_{0}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$. The initial data are
$$t_{0}:=0,\qquad x_{0}:=(r_{0},0,0),\qquad \mathbf v_{0}:=(u_{0},\Omega r_{0},0).$$
Then the constrained model with these data has the unique maximal constrained
motion
$$r(t):=Ae^{\Omega t}+Be^{-\Omega t},\qquad A:=\frac{r_{0}+u_{0}/\Omega}{2},\qquad B:=\frac{r_{0}-u_{0}/\Omega}{2},\qquad x(t):=r(t)\bigl(\cos\Omega t,\ \sin\Omega t,\ 0\bigr),$$
defined for all $t\in\mathbb R$, with multiplier, reaction and reaction power
$$\lambda(t)=\bigl(2m\Omega\,r'(t),\ mg\bigr),\qquad R(t)=2m\Omega\,r'(t)\,\bigl(-\sin\Omega t,\ \cos\Omega t,\ 0\bigr)+mg\,e_{3},\qquad R(t)\cdot x'(t)=2m\Omega^{2}r(t)r'(t),$$
kinetic energy $K(t)=\tfrac12m\bigl(r'(t)^{2}+\Omega^{2}r(t)^{2}\bigr)$ and
mechanical energy $E(t)=K(t)+mg\,z(t)=K(t)$ satisfying
$E'(t)=R(t)\cdot x'(t)=-\lambda(t)\cdot G_{t}(t,x(t))=2m\Omega^{2}r(t)r'(t)$;
the constraint is rheonomic, and the scleronomic conservation clause does not
apply. On the explicit model data
$$m=1\,\mathrm{kg},\quad \Omega=2\,\mathrm{s}^{-1},\quad r_{0}=1\,\mathrm m,\quad u_{0}=0\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1},\quad g=10\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}$$
one has $r(t)=\bigl(e^{2t}+e^{-2t}\bigr)/2\ \mathrm m$,
$E(t)=e^{4t}+e^{-4t}\ \mathrm J$ and $E'(t)=4\bigl(e^{4t}-e^{-4t}\bigr)\ \mathrm W$;
at $t=\tfrac12\,\mathrm s$, $E=\bigl(e^{2}+e^{-2}\bigr)\ \mathrm J\approx7.524391\,\mathrm J$
and $E'=4\bigl(e^{2}-e^{-2}\bigr)\ \mathrm W\approx29.014883\ \mathrm W$, so the mechanical
energy has strictly increased from its initial value $E(0)=2\ \mathrm J$ by
the work of the ideal reaction. All values are model values under the
declared idealizations, not measurements.
items.strategy: A worked model check: verify that the declared rotating-wire datum is a regular rheonomic holonomic constraint, that the displayed data are consistent and the explicit exponential-radius curve is the unique maximal constrained motion with the computed multiplier and reaction, that the reaction power equals 2 m Omega^2 r r' and the mechanical-energy balance holds with the rheonomic term only, and evaluate explicit model data with a strict energy increase.
items.physical_scope: A worked model check of the rheonomic ideal-constraint branch: one label of mass m constrained without friction to a straight wire through the origin that rotates uniformly in a horizontal plane, under the declared uniform downward field; the verification exhibits the unique maximal constrained motion through consistent data, computes the multiplier and the reaction, verifies the reaction-power identity and the mechanical-energy balance, and shows on explicit model data that an ideal rheonomic constraint performs positive work. The example is a model computation with declared idealizations (frictionless bead, massless rigid wire, prescribed uniform rotation, uniform field with the wire supporting the weight); every number is a model value, not a measurement.

items.title: The planar pendulum as an ideal holonomic model: the multiplier, the tension and the vanishing reaction power of a scleronomic constraint
items.statement:
Declare a one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ (coordinates
$(x,y,z)$, dimensions of [[def-cm01-units]]) and force map
$$F:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3}\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3},\qquad F(t,\mathbf x,\mathbf v):=(0,\,-mg,\,0),$$
where $[m]=\mu$ and the constant $g>0$ has dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$.
Let $l>0$ have dimension $\ell$, and use a dimensionless angle $\theta$ in
radians. Constrain the label,
without friction, to the circle of radius $l>0$ about the origin in the plane
$z=0$ --- the ideal pendulum realized as a bead threaded on a smooth circular
wire in a vertical plane --- by the regular holonomic-constraint datum
$$O:=\{(t,x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^{4}:(x,y)\ne(0,0)\},\qquad k:=2,\qquad G(t,x,y,z):=\bigl(x^{2}+y^{2}-l^{2},\ z\bigr)$$
of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]], and adopt the ideal-reaction law
of [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. The two constraint components have
dimensions $\ell^{2}$ and $\ell$. The locus is
$\Sigma=\{(t,l\sin\theta,-l\cos\theta,0):t,\theta\in\mathbb R\}$; write
$$X(\theta):=\bigl(l\sin\theta,\,-l\cos\theta,\,0\bigr),\qquad X_{\theta}(\theta):=\partial_{\theta}X(\theta)=\bigl(l\cos\theta,\,l\sin\theta,\,0\bigr),\qquad u(\theta):=\bigl(\sin\theta,\,-\cos\theta,\,0\bigr),\qquad X(\theta)=l\,u(\theta).$$

Then:

1. the datum is regular and scleronomic, the tangent vector $X_{\theta}(\theta)$
   is permitted for every $\theta$, and the virtual displacements at
   $X(\theta)$ are the line $\mathbb R\,X_{\theta}(\theta)$;
2. along any constrained motion the multiplier is
   $$\lambda(\theta,\theta')=\Bigl(-\frac{m}{2l}\bigl(g\cos\theta+l\,\theta'^{2}\bigr),\,0\Bigr)\in\mathbb R^{2}$$
   evaluated at the motion's data, the second component --- tied to the plane
   constraint $z=0$ --- vanishing along the motion, and the reaction is
   $$R=-T\,u(\theta),\qquad T=m\bigl(g\cos\theta+l\,\theta'^{2}\bigr),$$
   a force of magnitude $|T|$ along the line of the link, toward the pivot
   when $T>0$ (the **tension** of the model); the projection of the constrained
   equation on the tangent gives $ml^{2}\theta''+mgl\sin\theta=0$, and the
   projections on $u$ and on the normal $\mathbf e_{3}$ of the constraining
   plane give the displayed tension and the vanishing of the second multiplier
   component;
3. conversely, for every $C^{2}$ function $\theta:J\to\mathbb R$ with
   $ml^{2}\theta''+mgl\sin\theta=0$ on an interval $J$ with nonempty interior,
   the curve $x(t):=X(\theta(t))$ is a constrained motion of the model with
   multiplier and reaction as in clause 2;
4. the reaction power vanishes identically, $R\cdot x'\equiv0$, in agreement
   with the scleronomic case of the rheonomic-power theorem, and the
   mechanical energy $E=\tfrac12ml^{2}\theta'^{2}-mgl\cos\theta$ is constant
   along the motion; expressed through the energy,
   $T=3mg\cos\theta+2E/l$, and through the initial data $(\theta_{0},\theta_{0}')$,
   $T=mg(3\cos\theta-2\cos\theta_{0})+ml\,\theta_{0}'^{2}$;
5. for a motion with initial data at $t_{0}=0$ given by
   $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $l=1\,\mathrm m$,
   $g=10\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, $\theta_{0}=\pi/3$, $\theta_{0}'=0$, the
   initial energy is $E=-5\ \mathrm J$ and the tension is
   $T=30\cos\theta-10\ \mathrm N$, with $T=20\ \mathrm N$ at $\theta=0$ and
   $T=5\ \mathrm N$ at $\theta=\pi/3$, positive on the reachable arc
   $|\theta|\le\pi/3$.

All values are model values under the declared idealizations; the model is the
ideal pendulum realized by a smooth rigid wire (equivalently a massless link,
or a taut string while it stays taut), and the empirical qualifications are
recorded in the remarks.
items.strategy: A worked model check: verify the regular scleronomic circle datum, compute the multiplier and the reaction read as the tension, project the constrained equation to obtain the pendulum equation and the radial consistency condition, verify the converses on parametrized curves, check the identically vanishing reaction power and the conserved energy, and evaluate the tension formula on explicit model data.
items.physical_scope: A worked model check of the holonomic ideal-constraint branch: a mass point constrained without friction to a circle of radius l in a vertical plane about a fixed pivot under a declared uniform downward field, realized as a bead on a smooth circular wire, with the explicit two-component multiplier (the component tied to the constraining plane vanishing along the motion), the reaction read as the tension along the link, the standard pendulum equation obtained by projecting the constrained equation, the identically vanishing reaction power of the scleronomic constraint, and the conservation of the mechanical energy on explicit model data. The example is a model computation with the declared idealizations (smooth massless wire, equivalently a rigid link or a taut string while it stays taut; frictionless pivot; uniform field); every number is a model value, not a measurement, and the empirical status of a string that can go slack (or of a link that can buckle) is recorded as a limitation of the model.

items.title: All four inertial terms checked on explicit data, and the exact return to an inertial chart
items.statement:
Declare a one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, time
window $I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and the
**zero force map**
$$F:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3}\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3},\qquad F(t,\mathbf x,\mathbf v)\equiv0$$
(admissible: constant, hence of the standing regularity), in a fixed inertial frame $F$ with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$
([[post-cm01-frames]], [[def-cm01-units]]). For real parameters
$\omega_{0},\beta,\gamma$, vectors $a_{0},v_{c}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and
[[def-cm06-moving-frame]] data, take $\theta$ to be a dimensionless angle in
radians, with $[\omega_{0}]=\tau^{-1}$, $[\beta]=\tau^{-2}$,
$[\gamma]=\ell\tau^{-2}$, $[a_{0,j}]=\ell$ and
$[v_{c,j}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ for each spatial component $j$:
$$\theta(t):=\omega_{0}t+\tfrac12\beta t^{2},\qquad R(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta(t)&-\sin\theta(t)&0\\ \sin\theta(t)&\cos\theta(t)&0\\ 0&0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad c(t):=a_{0}+v_{c}t+\tfrac12\gamma t^{2}e_{1},$$
consider the motion $x(t):=x_{0}+v\,t$ of the zero-force model with
$x_{0}=(1,0,0)\,\mathrm m$, $v=(0,1,0)\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, its
moving-chart coordinate curve $y(t)=R(t)^{\mathsf T}(x(t)-c(t))$, and the
inertial-terms field
$\tau(t,y,\dot y)=-\bigl(2\omega(t)\times\dot y+\omega'(t)\times y+\omega(t)\times(\omega(t)\times y)+R(t)^{\mathsf T}c''(t)\bigr)$.

Then, for the parameter values $\omega_{0}=2\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
$\beta=1\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, $\gamma=3\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ and
$a_{0}=v_{c}=0$:

1. $R(t)\in SO(3)$ is $C^{\infty}$ and $\Omega=R^{\mathsf T}R'$ has the
   angular velocity $\omega(t)=\theta'(t)e_{3}=(2+t)e_{3}$ and
   $\omega'(t)=e_{3}$, while $c''(t)=(3,0,0)$;
2. $y(0)=e_{1}$, $\dot y(0)=-e_{2}$, and the moving-chart coordinate
   acceleration is $\ddot y(0)=-3e_{1}-e_{2}$ (in units
   $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}$); the inertial-chart acceleration is
   $\ddot x(t)=0$ for every $t$;
3. the four inertial terms at $t=0$ are $-2\omega\times\dot y=-4e_{1}$,
   $-\omega'\times y=-e_{2}$, $-\omega\times(\omega\times y)=+4e_{1}$ and
   $-R^{\mathsf T}c''=-3e_{1}$, and their sum is $\tau(0,y(0),\dot y(0))=-3e_{1}-e_{2}=\ddot y(0)$;
   clause 1 of [[pthm-cm06-inertial-forces]] therefore holds at $t=0$ for
   these data, with $m\ddot y=R^{\mathsf T}F+m\tau=m\tau$;
4. because $\omega\not\equiv0$, clause 3 of that theorem identifies the chart
   as **not** inertial; and with the alternative parameters
   $\omega_{0}=\beta=\gamma=0$, $a_{0}=(1,0,0)$,
   $v_{c}=(0,1,0)$, the chart has constant rotation $R\equiv I_{3}$ and affine
   reference curve, hence vanishing inertial terms, and the same motion has
   $\ddot y\equiv0$ in the chart, which is the inertial-frame description
   with $y(t)=x(t)-a_{0}-v_{c}t$.

All values are model values in the declared coordinates; the example reports
no measurement and asserts nothing about any apparatus.
items.strategy: A finite check: compute the chart quantities, evaluate all four inertial terms at one time on explicit data and compare with the chart acceleration of a uniform motion of the zero-force model, identify the chart as non-inertial through the criterion, and check an affine chart with constant rotation against the exact return to an inertial frame.
items.physical_scope: A worked finite check of the moving-chart equation of the framework: a zero-force one-label model observed in a chart with a uniformly accelerated rotation angle and a uniformly accelerated reference curve; the four inertial terms are evaluated term by term at one time and compared with the moving-chart coordinate acceleration of the motion, a chart with nonzero angular velocity is identified as non-inertial by the criterion, and an explicit chart with affine reference curve and constant rotation is checked to reproduce the inertial-frame description. All values are model values; the example reports no measurement.

items.title: Rolling as distinct models: the planar ideal no-slip disk against frictionless sliding, and the contact capability condition
items.statement:
Declare a **reduced planar disk model** on the two coordinates
$q=(x,\theta)\in\mathbb R^{2}$, where $x$ is the centre coordinate along a
straight line and $\theta$ the oriented spin, with the **declared kinetic
matrix**
$$M:=\begin{pmatrix}m&0\\ 0&I\end{pmatrix},\qquad m>0,\quad I>0,$$
of dimension $\mu$ and $\mu\ell^{2}$ respectively ([[def-cm01-units]]); the
reduction of a rigid disk to these two coordinates, with the spin inertia $I$
as model data, is a declared modelling step and is not derived here. The
applied generalized force is
$$\Phi:=(f,0),\qquad f\in\mathbb R,$$
a force $f$ on the centre and no applied spin torque, and the disk radius is
$a>0$. Here $[x]=[a]=\ell$, $[\theta]=1$ in radians, $[m]=\mu$,
$[I]=\mu\ell^{2}$, $[f]=\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$, and $[g]=\ell\tau^{-2}$;
the coefficient $\mu_s$ below is dimensionless. The two components of
$\Phi$ have dimensions of force and torque, respectively.

For the contact-capability comparison, additionally declare a horizontal
plane with scalar normal load $N=mg$, and the Coulomb static-contact capacity
model in which a signed tangential static reaction $f_s$ is available exactly
when $|f_s|\le\mu_sN$. Here $[N]=[f_s]=\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; this contact law
and its parameters are model assumptions, not measurements.

Consider two models of the planar contact, expressed in the same coordinates
and with the same $M$ and $\Phi$:

**(M1) ideal no-slip model.** The holonomic constraint
$$\mathcal G(x,\theta):=x-a\theta,\qquad \mathcal G_{q}=(1,-a),$$
imposed as $\mathcal G=0$; the Jacobian has rank one. With the d'Alembert
ideal-reaction law of
[[def-cm-holonomic-constraint-and-ideal-reactions]] and virtual displacements
$\delta\in\ker\mathcal G_{q}=\mathbb R(a,1)$: the generalized reaction is
$\mathcal G_{q}^{\mathsf T}\lambda$ for a multiplier $\lambda$, and the
motions satisfy $Mq''=\Phi+\mathcal G_{q}^{\mathsf T}\lambda$.

**(M2) frictionless sliding model.** No constraint and no reaction: the
motions satisfy $Mq''=\Phi$.

Then:

1. in **M1** the ideal motions satisfy
   $$\Bigl(m+\frac{I}{a^{2}}\Bigr)x''=f,\qquad x''=\frac{fa^{2}}{I+ma^{2}},\qquad \theta''=\frac{af}{I+ma^{2}},$$
   with the unique multiplier $\lambda=-\dfrac{fI}{I+ma^{2}}$, reaction
   $\mathcal G_{q}^{\mathsf T}\lambda=(\lambda,-a\lambda)$ and reaction power
   identically zero; the planar straight-line no-slip constraint is
   holonomic-equivalent, since $x-a\theta$ is constant along every admissible
   curve;
2. in **M2** the motions satisfy $x''=f/m$ and $\theta''=0$;
3. the two models make different predictions for the same applied force: for
   $f\ne0$ and $a^{2}m>0$,
   $$\frac{x''_{\mathrm{M1}}}{x''_{\mathrm{M2}}}=\frac{ma^{2}}{I+ma^{2}}=\frac{1}{1+I/(ma^{2})}<1,$$
   equal to $\tfrac23$ for a uniform thin disk $I=\tfrac12ma^{2}$ and to
   $\tfrac12$ for a hoop $I=ma^{2}$;
4. the ideal no-slip model requires the contact to supply the generalized
   reaction $(\lambda,-a\lambda)$, that is, a tangential contact force
   $f_{s}=\lambda$ of magnitude $|\lambda|=|f|I/(I+ma^{2})$ together with
   its torque. Adopt the Coulomb static-contact capacity model in which, for
   a declared normal load $N\ge0$ and dimensionless coefficient $\mu_{s}$,
   the available tangential static reactions satisfy exactly
   $|f_{s}|\le\mu_{s}N$; here declare $N=mg$ for a horizontal plane with
   weight-only vertical loading. Thus the no-slip idealization is feasible
   precisely while $|\lambda|\le\mu_{s}N$; for the uniform disk this is
   $|f|\le3\mu_{s}mg$. Where the required force exceeds the
   contact capability, the no-slip constraint cannot be maintained and a
   slipping model (with kinetic friction as a separately declared force)
   applies instead;
5. on the explicit model data $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $a=1\,\mathrm m$,
   $I=\tfrac12\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}$, $g=10\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}$
   and $f=3\,\mathrm N$: $x''_{\mathrm{M1}}=2\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}$,
   $x''_{\mathrm{M2}}=3\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}$,
   $\lambda=-1\,\mathrm N$ and $|\lambda|=1\,\mathrm N$, within
   $\mu_{s}N=5\,\mathrm N$ for the declared $\mu_{s}=\tfrac12$; with
   $f=18\,\mathrm N$ instead, M1 requires $|\lambda|=6\,\mathrm N>5\,\mathrm N$,
   so under those parameters the declared contact model cannot maintain the
   no-slip constraint and M1's premises fail.

All values are model values under the declared reduction and contact model;
the example reports no measurement.
items.strategy: A model-discrimination example: compare the reduced ideal no-slip model (holonomic constraint with ideal reaction) and the frictionless sliding model with the same declared kinetic matrix and applied force, computing the accelerations, multiplier, reaction and vanishing reaction power, deriving the ratio of the predictions, and evaluating the static-friction capability condition on explicit model data.
items.physical_scope: A worked model-discrimination example for the rolling contact: two reduced planar models of a disk with the same declared kinetic matrix and applied force — the ideal no-slip model with its holonomic constraint and ideal reaction, and the frictionless sliding model with no constraint — with the accelerations, the multiplier, the required contact force and a declared Coulomb static-friction capacity model compared on explicit model data. The example uses a reduced two-coordinate description declared as model data, asserts no measured value, and records that general three-dimensional rolling, slip transitions and contact changes are separate models outside it.
